summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's intrinsic behavior, tone, or output format consistently, or encode specialized domain knowledge and task patterns that prompting alone cannot reliably enforce. RAG is better when you need up-to-date or proprietary facts that change frequently, while prompt engineering suffices for most general tasks with clear instructions. In 2026 the landscape shifted notably: OpenAI is winding down its fine-tuning platform while Google (Vertex AI) and Anthropic (via Bedrock) remain primary managed options, and open-source frameworks like Unsloth, Axolotl, and LLaMA-Factory dominate self-hosted adoption.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, style, or tone that prompt engineering cannot reliably enforce across many requests.
Choose fine-tuning for specialized domain adaptation (legal, medical, financial) where the task patterns—not just facts—differ from the base model's training.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when your knowledge changes frequently or you need to cite up-to-date, proprietary documents at inference time.
Fine-tune only after prompting and RAG have been exhausted and you have a high-quality labeled dataset plus a clear, repeated task worth the training cost.

supported_models: select open models via Model Garden
tools.best_for: Enterprises adapting Gemini models with managed, closed-source fine-tuning

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Fine-tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-use for training tokens and provisioned throughput for custom models
features: Managed fine-tuning with region-varying model support
tools.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises fine-tuning and serving managed foundation models

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source (free); paid Pro/Enterprise tiers for multi-GPU and support
tools.best_for: Cost-efficient LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning on a single consumer GPU

tools.name: Together AI
tools.pricing_paid: Per-token/per-size fine-tuning; DPO costs ~2.5x supervised fine-tuning at each model size
tools.best_for: Fine-tuning and serving open-source models with fast managed inference

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source (free); compute costs depend on your infrastructure
features: Full, LoRA, QLoRA, and DPO support

tools.name: LLaMA-Factory
